title: Tamil song 'Varuvaaiy' earns Grammy nomination for Best Global Music Performance
dek: Devan Ekambaram and Susha's setting of a Subramania Bharati poem is among five nominees. RAYE leads the 2027 nominations with 11.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
"Varuvaaiy", a Tamil song by the Indian-American singer Devan Ekambaram featuring the Chennai-based vocalist Susha, has been nominated for Best Global Music Performance at the 69th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced on Monday. It is the first Grammy nomination for both singers, and Mr Ekambaram said on social media that it was "the very 1st Tamil Song to ever be nominated", a claim reported widely but not confirmed by the Academy. He described it as "a BHARATHIAR song", a setting of words by the Tamil poet Subramania Bharati; the instrumentalists Anil Srinivasan, Prakash Sontakke and Sarvajit Krishna also play on it.

It competes with "Una Flor En Cada Estrella" by KerreKe, Mireya and Alex E. Chávez, Angélique Kidjo's "Bando [Orchestral]" featuring Pharrell Williams and Quavo, Rosalía's "Porcelana" and "Dai Dai" by Shakira and Burna Boy, according to reports. The soundtrack of the Hindi film "Dhurandhar: The Revenge", which was submitted in nine categories, received no nominations, one report said.

The British singer RAYE leads this year's nominations with 11, followed by ROSALÍA with nine, and Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers with seven each, the Academy said. "It's a privilege to congratulate all the incredible music creators recognized in this year's Grammy nominations," said its chief executive, Harvey Mason jr. The ceremony is on 7 February 2027 at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, which is 5.30 am IST on 8 February.
